originality.rationale: The primary texts give question support, convex expressivity, and boundary antichain machinery but not the minimum common-domain person-cost distribution. The newly classified four-world histogram and its inquisitive semantics are not logical consequences of merely knowing the total number of convex subsets; every ten-bin value is obtained by two independent exhaustive constructions. The all-n extremal upper bound uses a credited classical theorem rather than being claimed as a new Sperner result. Historical priority beyond inspected sources remains uncertain.
residual_risks: An older unindexed table might enumerate minimum-plus-maximum boundary sizes in Boolean lattices and cover the histogram despite different terminology.
The structural all-n bound follows quickly from prior convex-set representation and a standard two-Sperner inequality; novelty is limited to the paired first-order semantics and weighted census.
Only material relevant portions of the long primary PDFs were inspected; no assertion of absolute priority or exhaustive global coverage.
